# Copy on Write Collections

`CopyOnWriteArrayList` and `CopyOnWriteArraySet` support thread-safe access and
snapshot iteration. They are useful when traversals vastly outnumber changes and
a reader needs a stable view without locking the traversal. The example
contrasts them with an unsafe concurrent access pattern using `ArrayList` and
`HashSet`.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this example, attendees can:

- explain how a snapshot iterator differs from a live view;
- distinguish the snapshot guarantee from fail-fast diagnostics and scheduling;
- identify the latch ordering and collection publication guarantees; and
- choose between copy-on-write collections and alternatives based on their
  operations, iteration semantics and write costs.

## Prerequisite

Install an
[Oracle Java 8](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java8) JDK
or newer and ensure `java` and `javac` resolve to it in your shell.

## The program to inspect

`Main` runs the list and set demonstrations in turn. Each first uses a
conventional collection, then a copy-on-write collection with the same tasks.

```java
package demo;

import static demo.utils.Logs.logHeaderAndJavaVersion;
import static demo.utils.Logs.logSection;

public final class Main {

    public static void main(final String[] args) {
        logHeaderAndJavaVersion("Copy on Write Collections");

        logSection("CopyOnWriteArrayList example");
        CopyOnWriteArrayListExample.run();

        logSection("CopyOnWriteArraySet example");
        CopyOnWriteArraySetExample.run();
    }
}
```

Each demonstration starts with ten cities. Three latches order the events:

1. The first reader creates its iterator, then releases the writer.
2. The writer adds Copenhagen with a `*` suffix, then releases the second reader.
3. The second reader creates its iterator, then releases the remaining writes.

For the copy-on-write collections, `->` therefore reads the original ten cities,
while `=>` reads those ten and `Copenhagen (Denmark)*`. Neither iterator sees
the later additions. Each iterator captures the backing array at its creation;
it is a snapshot, not a live view. List and copy-on-write set iteration follow
their respective iteration orders. Log lines may interleave differently, and
the latches do not guarantee that writes overlap the actual iteration. Sleeps
affect timing, not the guarantee.

The `ArrayList` and `HashSet` runs concurrently modify and iterate collections
without sufficient synchronisation. Their iterators may throw
`ConcurrentModificationException`, but fail-fast detection is best effort:
neither an exception nor a successful run makes that access pattern safe. In
particular, do not expect the same snapshot results for those runs.

The Java Memory Model (JMM) governs visibility and ordering of shared state. For
each latch, actions before `countDown()` happen-before actions after the
corresponding successful `await()`. In particular, the first addition
happens-before the second iterator is created. Separately, the concurrent
collections contract says actions before placing an object in the collection
happen-before another thread’s subsequent access or removal of that element.
Neither guarantee makes later unsynchronised mutations of an element safe. These
examples use immutable strings and do not demonstrate mutable-object
publication. The snapshot holds element references, not deep copies of objects.

`CompletableFuture.allOf(...).join()` waits for the tasks before reporting the
total, and the executor is shut down in `finally`. The log output illustrates
the snapshot; it is not proof of a memory-consistency guarantee.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Iterator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;
import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;
import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;
import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService;
import java.util.concurrent.Executors;
import java.util.function.Supplier;

import static demo.utils.Logs.log;
import static demo.utils.Logs.logError;
import static demo.utils.CountDownLatches.await;
import static demo.utils.Threads.sleepForAFewMilliseconds;
import static java.util.Objects.requireNonNull;

public final class CopyOnWriteArrayListExample {

    public static void run() {
        log("Concurrent read and write entries to ArrayList");
        log("This access pattern is unsafe; its iterator may fail fast");
        concurrentReadAndWrite(ArrayList::new);

        log("Concurrent read and write entries to CopyOnWriteArrayList");
        concurrentReadAndWrite(CopyOnWriteArrayList::new);
    }

    private static void concurrentReadAndWrite(final Supplier<List<String>> listConstructor) {
        requireNonNull(listConstructor, "The list constructor cannot be null");

        final List<String> cities = listConstructor.get();
        cities.add("Vienna (Austria)");
        cities.add("Brussels (Belgium)");
        cities.add("Paris (France)");
        cities.add("Berlin (Germany)");
        cities.add("Dublin (Ireland)");
        cities.add("Vaduz (Liechtenstein)");
        cities.add("Luxembourg City (Luxembourg)");
        cities.add("Monaco (Monaco)");
        cities.add("Amsterdam (Netherlands)");
        cities.add("Bern (Switzerland)");

        final CountDownLatch firstSnapshotTaken = new CountDownLatch(1);
        final CountDownLatch firstCityAdded = new CountDownLatch(1);
        final CountDownLatch secondSnapshotTaken = new CountDownLatch(1);

        /* Only in Java 19 the ExecutorService implements AutoClosable! */
        final ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(3);
        try {
            /* This reader takes a snapshot of the original 10 cities. */
            final CompletableFuture<Void> reader1 = CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> {
                        log("Printing Cities (->):");
                        final Iterator<String> snapshot = cities.iterator();
                        firstSnapshotTaken.countDown();
                        while (snapshot.hasNext()) {
                            final String city = snapshot.next();
                            log(" -> " + city);
                            sleepForAFewMilliseconds();
                        }
                    }, executor)
                    .exceptionally(throwable -> {
                        logError("Failed to read the list of cities (->)", throwable);
                        return null;
                    });

            final CompletableFuture<Void> writer = CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> {
                final String[] moreCities = {
                        "Copenhagen (Denmark)",
                        "Tallinn (Estonia)",
                        "Helsinki (Finland)",
                        "Reykjavik (Iceland)",
                        "Riga (Latvia)",
                        "Vilnius (Lithuania)",
                        "Oslo (Norway)",
                        "Stockholm (Sweden)",
                        "London (United Kingdom)"};

                log("Adding Cities (++):");
                await(firstSnapshotTaken);

                log(" ++ " + moreCities[0]);
                cities.add(moreCities[0] + '*'); /* Mark the new cities with a '*' */
                firstCityAdded.countDown();

                await(secondSnapshotTaken);
                for (int i = 1; i < moreCities.length; i++) {
                    final String city = moreCities[i];
                    log(" ++ " + city);
                    cities.add(city + '*'); /* Mark the new cities with a '*' */
                    sleepForAFewMilliseconds();
                }
            }, executor);

            /* This reader takes a snapshot containing the first added city. */
            final CompletableFuture<Void> reader2 = CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> {
                        log("Printing Cities (=>):");
                        await(firstCityAdded);
                        final Iterator<String> snapshot = cities.iterator();
                        secondSnapshotTaken.countDown();
                        while (snapshot.hasNext()) {
                            final String city = snapshot.next();
                            log(" => " + city);
                            sleepForAFewMilliseconds();
                        }
                    }, executor)
                    .exceptionally(throwable -> {
                        logError("Failed to read the list of cities (=>)", throwable);
                        return null;
                    });

            /* Wait for all tasks to complete */
            CompletableFuture.allOf(writer, reader1, reader2).join();

            log("Total number of cities: " + cities.size());
        } finally {
            executor.shutdown();
        }
    }
}
```

The set version uses the same coordination. `CopyOnWriteArraySet` uses an
internal `CopyOnWriteArrayList` and rejects duplicate elements.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.Iterator;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;
import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArraySet;
import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;
import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService;
import java.util.concurrent.Executors;
import java.util.function.Supplier;

import static demo.utils.Logs.log;
import static demo.utils.Logs.logError;
import static demo.utils.CountDownLatches.await;
import static demo.utils.Threads.sleepForAFewMilliseconds;
import static java.util.Objects.requireNonNull;

public final class CopyOnWriteArraySetExample {

    public static void run() {
        log("Concurrent read and write entries to HashSet");
        log("This access pattern is unsafe; its iterator may fail fast");
        concurrentReadAndWrite(HashSet::new);

        log("Concurrent read and write entries to CopyOnWriteArraySet");
        concurrentReadAndWrite(CopyOnWriteArraySet::new);
    }

    private static void concurrentReadAndWrite(final Supplier<Set<String>> setConstructor) {
        requireNonNull(setConstructor, "The set constructor cannot be null");

        final Set<String> cities = setConstructor.get();
        cities.add("Vienna (Austria)");
        cities.add("Brussels (Belgium)");
        cities.add("Paris (France)");
        cities.add("Berlin (Germany)");
        cities.add("Dublin (Ireland)");
        cities.add("Vaduz (Liechtenstein)");
        cities.add("Luxembourg City (Luxembourg)");
        cities.add("Monaco (Monaco)");
        cities.add("Amsterdam (Netherlands)");
        cities.add("Bern (Switzerland)");

        final CountDownLatch firstSnapshotTaken = new CountDownLatch(1);
        final CountDownLatch firstCityAdded = new CountDownLatch(1);
        final CountDownLatch secondSnapshotTaken = new CountDownLatch(1);

        /* Only in Java 19 the ExecutorService implements AutoClosable! */
        final ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(3);
        try {
            /* This reader takes a snapshot of the original 10 cities. */
            final CompletableFuture<Void> reader1 = CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> {
                        log("Printing Cities (->):");
                        final Iterator<String> snapshot = cities.iterator();
                        firstSnapshotTaken.countDown();
                        while (snapshot.hasNext()) {
                            final String city = snapshot.next();
                            log(" -> " + city);
                            sleepForAFewMilliseconds();
                        }
                    }, executor)
                    .exceptionally(throwable -> {
                        logError("Failed to read the list of cities (->)", throwable);
                        return null;
                    });

            final CompletableFuture<Void> writer = CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> {
                final String[] moreCities = {
                        "Copenhagen (Denmark)",
                        "Tallinn (Estonia)",
                        "Helsinki (Finland)",
                        "Reykjavik (Iceland)",
                        "Riga (Latvia)",
                        "Vilnius (Lithuania)",
                        "Oslo (Norway)",
                        "Stockholm (Sweden)",
                        "London (United Kingdom)"};

                log("Adding Cities (++):");
                await(firstSnapshotTaken);

                log(" ++ " + moreCities[0]);
                cities.add(moreCities[0] + '*'); /* Mark the new cities with a '*' */
                firstCityAdded.countDown();

                await(secondSnapshotTaken);
                for (int i = 1; i < moreCities.length; i++) {
                    final String city = moreCities[i];
                    log(" ++ " + city);
                    cities.add(city + '*'); /* Mark the new cities with a '*' */
                    sleepForAFewMilliseconds();
                }
            }, executor);

            /* This reader takes a snapshot containing the first added city. */
            final CompletableFuture<Void> reader2 = CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> {
                        log("Printing Cities (=>):");
                        await(firstCityAdded);
                        final Iterator<String> snapshot = cities.iterator();
                        secondSnapshotTaken.countDown();
                        while (snapshot.hasNext()) {
                            final String city = snapshot.next();
                            log(" => " + city);
                            sleepForAFewMilliseconds();
                        }
                    }, executor)
                    .exceptionally(throwable -> {
                        logError("Failed to read the list of cities (=>)", throwable);
                        return null;
                    });

            /* Wait for all tasks to complete */
            CompletableFuture.allOf(writer, reader1, reader2).join();

            log("Total number of cities: " + cities.size());
        } finally {
            executor.shutdown();
        }
    }
}
```

Copy-on-write mutations are costly because they generally copy the underlying
array. Long-lived iterators can also retain old arrays. These collections suit
read-heavy workloads such as listener lists or small sets of handlers, where
infrequent changes and snapshot traversal are acceptable. Iterator mutation is
unsupported. Individual thread-safe operations do not make a sequence of
operations atomic, and the API does not promise fairness.

A `ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet()` can be considered for a set with frequent
updates when weakly consistent iteration is acceptable instead of snapshots. A
`ConcurrentLinkedQueue` serves FIFO producer-consumer workloads, but is not a
general replacement for indexed list operations. Choose by the operations and
iteration guarantees required; this example is not a benchmark.

2. Build the application and create the JAR file.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) List the created JAR file.

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file

   ```
   ./target/libs
   └── copy-on-write-collections-1.0.0.jar

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

   Run the application.

   ```shell
   java \
     -classpath './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main
   ```

   One possible run; task and log ordering will vary.
